ideas.title: Lockstep Canals
ideas.novelty: Legal tile-to-tile connection is decided entirely by comparing carved edge notch counts (a 'water level' 0-3) that must match or differ by exactly one, so the drafting/placement rule itself is physically readable and self-enforcing from the carved geometry rather than from a rulebook table. Search run: 'board game canal tile laying edge notch water level lock matching' surfaced classic edge-matching connection games (Tantrix/Serpentiles, Oceania) that match colour or land/water type across edges, but none use a graduated notch-count level-difference rule for a lock mechanic.
ideas.concept: 2-4 players draft carved lock-stones from a shared market and extend a stone canal outward from their own spring, obeying a simple physical rule: a new stone's grooved edge may only join a placed neighbour's grooved edge if the tally notches cut into each edge match or differ by exactly one. One turn is a quick market pick, a legality check by eye and touch, and a placement; the tension is drafting stones whose levels will still connect to your growing network later.

art_direction.form_language: Thick quarry-cut stone slabs with chiselled water channels and heavy 2mm 45-degree chamfered edges throughout, reading as hand-tooled canal masonry, never as a flat printed board.
art_direction.silhouette: A sunken square stone basin with four small spouts projecting from its outer edges, ringed by a scatter of loose carved lock-stones and a stubby loading sill of five cupped slots, like a mason's yard mid-project rather than a game box.
art_direction.part_vocabulary: Canal board = a sunken basin block whose grid is a field of shallow square sockets with a scoop bin let into one corner. Lock-stones = flat quarried slabs, each cut with a single trench connecting two, three, or four edges to a center hub, with a row of tally notches along every grooved edge counting its water level; the trench pattern alone tells straight from corner from tee from cross at a glance. Font-stones (4) = the player spring markers, distinguished from ordinary lock-stones by a round scooped basin at the center and a punched row of 1-4 owner holes near one corner, reading as a mason's signature mark. Loading sill = a shallow ledged plank with five cupped slots, reading as a presentation rail, not a tray.
art_direction.surface_treatment: Channel trench 5mm wide x 3mm deep with a rounded floor; tally notches 2mm wide x 1.5mm deep triangular cuts spaced 3mm apart along a grooved edge's rim; all outer edges of every stone carry a 2mm x 45-degree chamfer so the trench and notches read as deliberately tooled relief, not machine-flat.
art_direction.scale: Board footprint approx 366 x 366 x 15mm including the four edge spurs; lock-stones and font-stones are 40 x 40 x 8mm, comfortably a one-hand pinch; the corner draw bin is an open-topped 170 x 90 x 36mm pocket for a loose reserve, reached from directly above with nothing overhanging it.
art_direction.hero_shot: Overhead three-quarter shot showing the basin board mid-game with several connected lock-stones forming a visible carved channel from one font-stone toward the board edge, notch counts readable along the seams, loose stones and the five-slot loading sill beside it.

ideas.rules: Players: 2-4. Setup: place the canal board centrally. Each player takes the font-stone matching their assigned owner-hole count (1, 2, 3, or 4 holes) and seats it in the matching spur well at the board's edge. Shuffle the 36 lock-stones and place them loose in the corner draw bin. Draw 5 lock-stones from the bin and seat one in each of the five loading-sill slots, face up. The player with the fewest owner holes goes first; turns proceed clockwise. On your turn: choose one lock-stone from the loading sill and seat it into any empty grid well that is orthogonally adjacent to a stone already on the board (a font-stone counts as already on the board). The placement is legal only if: (a) at least one of the new stone's grooved edges lines up with a grooved edge of an already-placed neighbour, and (b) for every such grooved-to-grooved alignment, the two stones' notch counts are equal or differ by exactly 1. A grooved edge lining up against a plain (ungrooved) neighbour edge is allowed and simply seals with no water link. After placing, immediately refill the loading sill from the draw bin. If you cannot legally place any of the 5 sill stones, discard one sill stone of your choice to the side and pass. The game ends when the draw bin and loading sill are both empty and no player has a legal placement, or the grid is full. Scoring: for each player, trace the single longest unbroken chain of grooved-to-grooved links starting at their own font-stone. Score 1 point per stone in that chain, plus 1 bonus point for every link in the chain where the two notch counts were exactly equal (a level pour) rather than differing by 1 (a lock). Highest total score wins; ties favour the player with fewer owner holes.
ideas.components: 1 canal board (approx 366 x 366 x 15mm): a rigid slab with a 6x6 grid of 36 square wells (each 42 x 42 x 4mm deep on a 44mm pitch), one 42 x 42 x 4mm spur well projecting from the midpoint of each of the four outer edges, and an open-topped rectangular draw bin (170 x 90 x 36mm interior) recessed into one corner. 36 lock-stones (40 x 40 x 8mm each): four shape families told apart purely by which edges carry a carved trench to the center hub - Straight (9, two opposite edges), Corner (9, two adjacent edges), Tee (9, three edges), Cross (9, all four edges); each family exists in three level variants (1, 2, or 3 tally notches cut into every grooved edge of that stone), three copies per shape-and-level combination (4 shapes x 3 levels x 3 copies = 36). 4 font-stones (40 x 40 x 8mm each): one grooved edge at level 0 (no notches) leading to an 8mm-diameter, 3mm-deep scooped reservoir at the tile center, plus 1-4 pierced 3mm-diameter owner holes near the corner opposite the grooved edge, one count per player. 1 loading sill (240 x 60 x 12mm): a plank with five 44 x 44 x 3mm square cupped slots spaced 46mm apart, holding the face-up market row.

must_survive.feature: The board, the loading sill, and all 40 stones (36 lock-stones + 4 font-stones) exist as 42 separate, freely liftable components, not fused into the board or into each other.
must_survive.visual: iso_front: 40 individually distinguishable stones sitting loose in the board's wells and the sill's slots, each with a visible gap at its edges, not a continuous poured slab.

must_survive.feature: Each font-stone carries the correct count of pierced owner holes, so player ownership is readable by hole count alone.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z close-up on font-stone D: 4 distinct pierced through-holes in a row near one corner, clearly separate from the tile's grooved edge and center basin.

must_survive.feature: A representative lock-stone carries the full tally-notch count its level and shape require, so water level is readable by notch count alone.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z close-up on one cross-shaped, level-3 lock-stone: all four grooved edges each show 3 separate triangular notch cuts along the rim.

must_survive.feature: The loading sill has 5 distinct cupped slots capable of seating one stone each.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z on the loading sill: 5 separate square depressions in a row, each large enough to seat a lock-stone with a visible surrounding lip.

must_survive.feature: The corner draw bin is a genuine open cavity a hand can reach into, not filled solid.
must_survive.visual: iso_front on the board's corner bin: an open rectangular pocket with a visible interior floor and side walls, no material blocking the top opening.

ideas.prompt: Product photo of a tabletop canal-building game: a large square stone-toned board (~370mm) with a sunken 6x6 grid of square recessed wells, four small spout wells projecting from the middle of each outer edge, and an open rectangular scoop bin let into one corner holding a loose jumble of flat carved tiles. Scattered across the board and beside it are dozens of flat 40mm square lock-stones, each carved with a single trench connecting two, three, or four edges to a center hub point, with small triangular tally notches cut along every grooved edge (one, two, or three notches per edge, clearly countable). Four special corner stones show a round scooped basin at center and a short row of punched circular holes near one corner. A narrow rectangular plank with five shallow square cups sits beside the board holding five face-up stones. Unpainted single material, sharp studio lighting, isometric three-quarter product angle, focus on the carved channel and notch relief.

ideas.title: Sluice Row
ideas.novelty: Twist on Mancala (Kalah): standard Kalah pits have unlimited practical capacity and every seed counts equally; here every small pit carries an engraved capacity ring, and once a pit's seed pile reaches that ring it becomes physically 'full' and is skipped entirely during sowing, while seeds themselves come in three graduated sizes worth different scoring values, so final scoring is total seed value, not seed count. Search run: 'mancala variant seeds different sizes pit capacity limit skip full pit' found only conventional Kalah variants changing pit/seed counts or relay-sowing rules; none combine a physical fill-line skip rule with graduated seed values.
ideas.concept: A two-row sowing race played exactly like classic Kalah, except the pits themselves push back: once a pit's pile reaches its engraved gauge line it is skipped during sowing, forcing players to route around their own bottlenecks, and the three sizes of seed-weights mean a captured pit full of small seeds is worth far less than one big seed.

art_direction.form_language: A single heavy timber-plank slab with deep dished basins and a soft rolled bullnose edge, reading as an antique grain-weighing trough rather than a printed mancala board.
art_direction.silhouette: A long low trough-board with two oversized end cisterns and a tidy row of small round wells between them, like an old measuring device set out on a table.
art_direction.part_vocabulary: Board = a measuring trough, its two end wells scaled up and unmarked to read as cisterns, its twelve middle wells uniform in size but each ringed with a fine engraved gauge line. Seeds = grain-weights, three graduated squat cylinder families (short, wide vs narrow) that read as a nested set of measuring weights, not tokens - the diameter alone marks its value.
art_direction.surface_treatment: Each small well's interior wall carries a 1mm-wide, 0.5mm-deep engraved gauge ring at a fixed height from the floor; every well opening carries a 2mm rounded fillet so the rim reads as worn-smooth rather than machined-sharp.
art_direction.scale: Board approx 380 x 170 x 24mm; small wells 26mm diameter x 16mm deep; end cisterns 55mm diameter x 20mm deep; seeds range 10-18mm diameter, all 7mm tall, each easily pinched between two fingers.
art_direction.hero_shot: Straight-on three-quarter shot along the trough's long axis showing both end cisterns, the row of gauge-ringed wells between them, and a mix of the three seed-weight sizes both loose beside the board and piled in a couple of wells up to their gauge line.

ideas.rules: Players: 2. Setup: the board has two rows of 6 small wells facing each player, plus one store well at each end belonging to the player on that side. Shuffle 48 seed-weights (16 small, value 1; 16 medium, value 2; 16 large, value 3) and place 4 at random into each of the 12 small wells. Stores start empty. Turn: on your turn, pick a non-empty well on your own side (you may pick up a full well; picking it up always empties it), lift out every seed-weight in it, and sow them one at a time counter-clockwise into each following well in turn, including your own store but skipping your opponent's store entirely, and skipping any well that is currently full (its pile at or above its gauge ring) as if that well did not exist. If your very last sown seed-weight lands in an empty well on your own side and the well directly opposite it (on your opponent's side) contains any seed-weights, capture: move every seed-weight from that opposite well plus your last sown seed-weight into your own store. If your last sown seed-weight lands in your own store, take another turn. The game ends the instant a player's entire row is empty at the start of their turn; the other player then sweeps every remaining seed-weight on their own side into their own store. Scoring: sum the VALUE (not the count) of every seed-weight in your store (small=1, medium=2, large=3). Whoever has the higher total value wins; equal totals are a draw.
ideas.components: 1 trough board (approx 380 x 170 x 24mm) with 12 small wells (2 rows of 6, each 26mm diameter x 16mm deep, with a 1mm x 0.5mm engraved capacity ring 9mm up from the floor) and 2 store wells (one at each short end, 55mm diameter x 20mm deep, no capacity ring). 48 seed-weights: 16 small cylinders (10mm diameter x 7mm tall, value 1), 16 medium cylinders (14mm diameter x 7mm tall, value 2), 16 large cylinders (18mm diameter x 7mm tall, value 3) - all equal height so pile height against the gauge ring is a reliable visual cue regardless of which sizes fill a well.

must_survive.feature: The board and all 48 seed-weights exist as 49 discrete, freely liftable components, not fused into the board floor or into each other.
must_survive.visual: iso_front: 48 individually distinguishable loose seed-weights sitting in the wells with visible gaps between adjacent pieces, not a solid poured mass.

must_survive.feature: Every small well carries its own visible engraved capacity ring, distinct from the well's rim.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z close-up on one small well: a clear engraved ring line partway down the interior wall, separate from the well's outer rim edge.

must_survive.feature: The full set of 16 small-diameter seed-weights is present and distinguishable by diameter from the medium and large sets.
must_survive.visual: iso_front on a loose cluster of seed-weights: three clearly different cylinder diameters visible side by side, all the same height.

must_survive.feature: Two store wells exist and are visibly larger than the twelve small wells.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z whole board: two markedly larger circular wells at the two ends versus the twelve uniform smaller wells between them.

must_survive.feature: The largest seed-weight sits inside a small well with genuine finger clearance rather than a press fit.
must_survive.visual: iso_front close-up: one large seed-weight resting inside a small well with a visible gap ring between the seed's edge and the well wall.

ideas.prompt: Product photo of a tabletop mancala-style game: a long low rectangular trough board (~380x170mm) with two rows of six small round dished wells between two much larger round end wells. Inside each small well a fine engraved ring line is visible partway down the interior wall. Scattered in and around the wells are small stout cylindrical seed-weights in three clearly different diameters (roughly 10mm, 14mm, and 18mm) all the same short height, some piled loosely inside a couple of wells up to the engraved ring line. Unpainted single material, soft studio lighting, isometric three-quarter angle, close enough to read the engraved gauge ring inside one open well.

ideas.title: Tidepool Stones
ideas.novelty: Reskin of Othello/Reversi with no rule change: ownership, normally carried by a black/white disc face, is instead carried by two distinct carved relief motifs on the same disc's two faces (concentric rings vs radial grooves), so flipping a disc physically swaps which motif is exposed exactly as it would swap colour. Search run: 'Othello Reversi wooden disc reskin textured relief instead of black white' found only conventional black/white or wood-species (walnut vs maple) commercial sets; no textured dual-relief disc adaptation for the no-colour case.
ideas.concept: Standard Reversi play, restyled as a beachcombed tidepool: every disc is a thick stone lens carved with concentric barnacle rings on one face and a radiating mussel-shell fan on the other, seated in a scalloped stone basin. Flipping a captured disc turns the shell over, exactly the way Reversi always worked, just carried by carved relief instead of paint.

art_direction.form_language: A low tide-pool basin slab with a grid of shallow scalloped hollows, each cradling a thick biconvex-edged stone lens; everything reads as beach-worn rock, no flat plastic sheen implied.
art_direction.silhouette: A square tide-pool slab studded with 64 fat pebble-lenses sitting in individual scooped hollows, like a collected tray of shells rather than an abstract board.
art_direction.part_vocabulary: Board = a tide basin, its grid carried by raised dividing ridges between hollows rather than printed lines. Discs = shell-lenses, a single thick biconvex-profile puck family where one face is carved with concentric barnacle rings and the reverse with a radiating mussel-shell fan - both motifs live on every disc, so ownership reads from which face is up, not from a second part.
art_direction.surface_treatment: Ridge face: 4 concentric engraved rings, 1mm wide x 0.8mm deep, spaced 2mm apart, centered on the disc. Fan face: 8 straight radial grooves, 1mm wide x 0.8mm deep, fanning evenly from center to rim. Board grid ridges stand 2mm proud between hollows with a 1mm fillet.
art_direction.scale: Board approx 260 x 260 x 18mm; discs 28mm diameter x 7mm tall, seated in 30mm-diameter x 3mm-deep hollows so each disc sits 4mm proud of the surrounding ridge for an easy two-finger pinch-and-flip.
art_direction.hero_shot: Overhead three-quarter shot of the full basin mid-game, most hollows filled, with two adjacent discs deliberately shown mid-flip (one ring-face-up, one fan-face-up beside it) so both carved motifs are legible in the same frame.

ideas.rules: Players: 2, Ridge and Fan. Setup: place the tide basin between players. Seed the four center hollows in the standard Reversi diagonal pattern: two discs Ridge-face-up and two discs Fan-face-up, arranged so each player's two starting discs sit diagonally opposite each other. Ridge moves first. Turn: on your turn, place one disc from the shared supply, your face up, into any empty hollow such that it forms at least one straight line (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) in which your placed disc and an existing disc of your face at the far end sandwich one or more consecutive opposing-face discs with no empty hollow between them. Turn over (flip) every sandwiched opposing disc in place so your face now shows on top of each. If you have no legal placement, you pass and play continues with your opponent; if neither player has a legal placement, the game ends. The game also ends when the basin is full. Whichever face shows on more discs at game end wins; equal counts are a draw.
ideas.components: 1 tide basin board (approx 260 x 260 x 18mm) with an 8x8 grid of 64 shallow circular hollows (each 30mm diameter x 3mm deep on a 32mm pitch), separated by a continuous raised dividing ridge standing 2mm proud between adjacent hollows. 64 shell-lens discs (28mm diameter x 7mm tall each): every disc identical, with one face carved with 4 concentric engraved rings (Ridge face) and the opposite face carved with 8 straight radial grooves fanning from center to rim (Fan face).

must_survive.feature: The board and all 64 discs exist as 65 discrete, freely liftable components, not fused into the board or into each other.
must_survive.visual: iso_front: 64 individually distinguishable loose discs sitting in the basin's hollows with a visible gap around each disc's edge, not fused to the board or to each other.

must_survive.feature: The Ridge face of a disc carries the correct count of concentric engraved rings.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z close-up on one disc's Ridge face: 4 clearly separated concentric engraved rings centered on the disc.

must_survive.feature: The Fan face of the same disc carries the correct count of radial grooves.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z close-up on the same disc flipped over: 8 straight grooves radiating evenly from center to rim.

must_survive.feature: The board presents 64 distinct hollows separated by a continuous raised grid ridge, not a smooth flat plate.
must_survive.visual: ortho_TOP_+Z whole board: an 8x8 grid of round recessed hollows with visible raised ridges running between them.

must_survive.feature: A disc seated in its hollow has enough radial clearance to be pinched and flipped by hand, not a press fit.
must_survive.visual: iso_front close-up: one disc resting in its hollow, standing proud of the surrounding ridge with a visible edge gap for a fingertip pinch.

ideas.prompt: Product photo of a tabletop abstract strategy game: a flat square basin board (~260mm) with an 8x8 grid of shallow round scalloped hollows separated by thin raised dividing ridges, most hollows holding a thick lens-shaped disc standing proud of the ridges. Several visible discs show a face carved with four concentric rings like a target; a couple of discs nearby are shown propped on edge or mid-flip revealing the reverse face carved with eight straight radial grooves fanning from center to rim like a shell. Unpainted single material, isometric three-quarter product angle, sharp studio lighting, focus on the two contrasting carved disc faces side by side.
